en.html:
I introduced myself as Shirou Kuniuji's messenger and requested a meeting with Sakurako Okabe. The Kyougoku household was not expecting this item of business. Their faces made that clear.

I conveyed Kuniuji's wish to keep the matter small also. They let me through, but small was probably not how it would remain.

Still, better than Kuniuji Ashikaga arriving himself without warning. And sneaking in was hardly an option. What else to do? Some discreet questioning would probably go in his direction now.

Surely he understood that. Understanding it, he had wanted this all the same.

en.html:
I was shown to a room at the back. There Princess Sakurako waited in a deep bow. The seat of honour had been left empty.

...For the present I was, after all, the representative of the General of the Left Imperial Guard, so the treatment was only proper. The honour belonged to him. The sitting would have to be done by me. Somehow these two facts were expected to fit on the same cushion.

A moment ago I had been carrying a flowerpot. Now a princess was bowing. Bhai, let me put the flower down before adding the whole court hierarchy. Neither my hands nor my understanding had been prepared for this weight.

en.html:
I sat down where convenient and briefly explained this peculiar connection with Kuniuji. Quite a story, agreed. But she had seen the noble boy playing football herself. That helped the explanation stand on its feet.

While speaking, I let my eyes take in the room. No iron bars. No little slit of a window grudgingly allowing light. An ordinary room only.

Even if it was not her personal chamber, she seemed sufficiently at home for me to think it part of her living quarters. Her conditions, then, did not appear so severe. Walks were apparently permitted also, as we had seen.

...This leniency, however, was hardly out of concern for her health and happiness.

Rokuhara feared contact between Princess Sakurako and the anti-shogunate forces. That was why they had put her here in Fudaraku. But they must also be hoping for the same thing. Let both sides make contact and act; then catch the whole lot in one net.

A little less guarding around her, what difference? Escape from this castle was impossible anyway. Why waste vigilance when they could make her bait for a bigger catch? Bloody calculating bastards. Even their leniency had teeth.

ja.html:
適当に座って、俺は邦氏との奇縁を手短に説明した。
　妙といえば随分と妙な話であった筈だが、あの高貴
な少年が蹴球を嗜む様は彼女も目撃していたので理解
させるに難は無かった。

　話しつつ、視線を流して部屋の様子を観察する。
　別に鉄格子で囲われている事はないし、窓が明かり
取りの小窓だけなどという事もない。

　普通の部屋だった。
　ここが彼女の居室ではないにしても、部屋に慣れた
様子からして居住空間の一部であるのは確かと思える。
となると、姫の環境はそう厳しいものでも無さそうだ。

　先日の通り、散歩なども許されているらしい。
　
　……だがこの緩やかな待遇は、決して彼女の心身の
健康を思いやっての事ではないだろう。

　六波羅は桜子姫と反幕勢力との接触を警戒している。
なればこそこの普陀楽に置いたのだ。
　しかし一方で期待もしている筈だ――両者が接触し
行動を起こせば、一網打尽だと。

　桜子の身辺を手薄にしてもさして問題はない。<ruby>結局<rt>・・</rt></ruby>
<ruby>のところ<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>、この城内から脱出するなど不可能だからだ。
　必要もない厳戒態勢を捨て、大魚を誘い出す釣り餌
としている。全く、六波羅はいちいち狡猾であった。

Perhaps Ichijou's words the other day had come back to her.

en.html:
An outrageous thing to say, if one considered it. The Ashikaga heir on one side, the surviving Okabe daughter on the other. Their positions were so different, even making the comparison was foolishness.

But Princess Sakurako did not reject it straightaway. She lowered her gaze to the stock and considered.

Was she remembering that brief encounter, hardly more than passing each other...?

Looking into her eyes, I thought I could see the boy's flushed cheeks.

Looking into her eyes, I thought I could see the boy's flushed cheeks.

en.html:
Bas, no more explanation. Beyond facts I did not want to go. I had not come here to talk her into something.

That boy, and the shadow over him, gave me much else to think about. But what use, passing my thoughts from my mouth into her ears?

When she came to know for herself, then it would be real. And perhaps that knowing was not very far away.

I answered only by lowering my head.

Simple it would not be. Suppose both of them wanted it. Would the people around them permit it? No. Hardly any chance.

The road might become harder than going alone. Even knowing that, if they chose to walk beside each other...

Not so lonely. Compared with being alone, at least a little of that cold would lessen.

en.html:
Full postman I had become. Kya karein, the return journey was now included.

Idhar ka dil udhar, udhar ka jawaab idhar. Carry this heart over there, bring that heart's answer back here. The two noble people would sit in their respective rooms while my legs conducted the relationship. Such an elevated form of human connection.

If this developed into a quarrel, carrying messages would be the worst possible duty. Each side could sharpen the words at leisure. I would have to hold them by the sharp end, bow, and announce whose compliments they came with.
